Fraud awareness, evidence & digital safety

FINDAT Security Window

Understand how financial and technology fraud works, see the scale of the risk through credible data, and learn a practical verification routine for suspicious calls, messages, links, payment requests and online offers.

Africa fraud and cyber-risk data snapshot

These indicators come from separate INTERPOL and GSMA datasets. They explain the size of the digital economy and the pressure created by online scams, account takeover, business-email compromise and other cyber-enabled fraud.

Why mobile-money vigilance matters

Digital finance has enormous reach, so a single stolen PIN, SIM or one-time code can expose real savings.

50%of accounts
1.75Bregistered mobile-money accounts worldwide
$1.4Tprocessed through mobile money each year

GSMA reports that Sub-Saharan Africa is home to half of the world’s mobile-money accounts.

Finance fraud awareness

Protect your money and payment credentials

Financial fraud often begins with an urgent call, fake investment, altered payment instruction or request for a PIN or one-time code. Genuine institutions should be verified through contact details you found independently.

  • Bank and mobile-money impersonationFraudsters pretend to be staff and ask you to “reverse,” “confirm” or “secure” a transaction.
  • Investment and cryptocurrency scamsGuaranteed returns, secret opportunities and pressure to deposit quickly are major warning signs.
  • Invoice and payment redirectionA changed account number or mobile-money line must be confirmed through a known contact.
  • Fake loans, prizes and refundsAdvance fees, “processing charges” and requests to pay before receiving money are common traps.
Photo: RDNE Stock project via Pexels.
Technology fraud awareness

Protect your identity, devices and accounts

Technology-enabled fraud uses convincing websites, messages, caller IDs, QR codes and AI-generated voices or images. Familiar branding or a realistic profile does not prove that a request is genuine.

  • Phishing, smishing and QR-code trapsLinks or attachments may lead to fake sign-in pages, malware or requests for personal information.
  • Account takeover and OTP theftAnyone asking for your password, PIN, one-time code or approval notification is a serious warning sign.
  • Fake technical supportUnexpected claims that your phone or computer has a virus may lead to requests to install remote-access software.
  • AI impersonation and deepfakesA realistic voice, video or profile can be fabricated. Confirm urgent requests through a separate trusted channel.
Photo: Christina Morillo via Pexels.

How a typical fraud attempt develops

Recognising the sequence helps you interrupt the fraud before information or money is transferred.

1. ContactAn unexpected call, message, email or social-media approach.
2. PressureUrgency, fear, secrecy or a promise of fast profit.
3. InformationA request for a PIN, password, OTP, ID or account details.
4. PaymentMoney is sent to a changed, unfamiliar or personal account.
5. DisappearanceThe contact blocks you, delays, or demands another payment.

How to stay vigilant

Use this six-step routine before trusting a financial or technology request.

Slow downUrgency and fear are tools used to stop you from thinking. End the call or pause the conversation.
Verify independentlyUse an official app, card, statement or website you found yourself—not a link or number supplied in the message.
Keep secrets privateNever share passwords, PINs, CVV numbers, one-time codes or security answers. Legitimate staff should not request them.
Secure your accountsUse unique passwords, multi-factor authentication and current software updates. Lock your SIM and phone where supported.
Check the transactionConfirm the recipient name, account or mobile number, amount and reason before approving any payment.
Report quicklyContact the bank, mobile-money provider or platform immediately. Preserve screenshots, numbers, messages and transaction references.

60-second fraud check

Select every warning sign present in the request you received.

No assessment has been run. When uncertain, stop and verify through an official channel.

Think you may have been targeted?

Do not send more money or pay anyone who promises to recover lost funds. Contact the relevant bank or service provider using official contact details, change exposed passwords, review recent transactions and file a cyber complaint. For identity theft in Zambia, ZICTA advises contacting your bank and reporting to the Police.

Report to ZICTA Identity-theft guidance

x1 — financial reconciliation made visible

x1 brings transaction preparation, matching, exception review and report governance into one workflow. The uploaded Flask application includes account access, subscriptions, CSV/XLSX processing, bank reconciliation, report history, signatories and AI-assisted transaction review.

  • Compare bank statements with cash-ledger records.
  • Separate matched and unmatched transactions.
  • Produce an accountant-style Bank Reconciliation Statement with updated Bank and Cash Accounts.
  • Maintain reports, approvals and audit evidence.

What x1 can do

The showcase below is based on the functions and workflows present in the uploaded application. Production deployment requires secure server configuration, tested integrations and controlled user access.

Functional scope

Data transformation

Accept CSV/XLSX records, standardise column names, clean dates and currency values, and prepare structured transaction files.

Automated reconciliation

Compare cash debits with bank credits and cash credits with bank debits using one-to-one amount matching.

Exception detection

Identify deposits in transit, outstanding payments, bank collections and service charges from unmatched records.

Accountant-ready statements

Generate a complete Bank Reconciliation Statement, Updated Bank Account and Updated Cash Account with supporting schedules and a clear reconciliation conclusion.

Review and approval

Support prepared-by, reviewed-by and approved-by roles, signatory records and controlled report status changes.

AI-assisted review

Submit bank and cash data for anomaly summaries, matched/unmatched analysis and conversational follow-up.

1. UploadBank and cash records are supplied in supported formats.
2. PrepareDates, IDs and financial values are cleaned and standardised.
3. MatchCorresponding debit and credit values are paired.
4. ReviewUnmatched transactions become reconciliation exceptions.
5. ReportResults are documented, reviewed, approved and retained.

Explore our work

FINDAT Consultants is a technological innovation practice centred on applied financial research, data design and automation, and knowledge management.

Our aim is to help organisations turn financial evidence, operational records and institutional knowledge into practical systems for better decisions.

We provide applied financial research, data architecture, dashboard design, knowledge products, automation workflows and professional training for businesses, public institutions, NGOs and development partners.

Our teams combine financial research, data design, automation, technology implementation and knowledge management to produce clear, usable and decision-ready solutions.
